messages:
marie: Heads-up — canary pool in us-west-2 started failing right after we flipped the default container to toolkit-12. Nodes are restarting and we see NCCL/connect errors from the serving pods. Rolling back or hotfix?

deploy-bot: Started canary rollout rwd/cuda12-toolkit:2026-03-16 -> 12 nodes in us-west-2 (canary-3). See https://ci.internal/deploy/987

jason: Copy. Any kernel oops or missing symbols in the logs? Can you paste a short excerpt?

marie: Here's the typical crash from a failed pod:
```
[2026-03-16T14:21:03Z] runtime: failed to load libstdc++ from container
/opt/conda/envs/runner/bin/python: /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libstdc++.so.6: version `GLIBCXX_3.4.29' not found (required by /usr/local/cuda-12.0/lib64/libcudart.so)
NCCL WARN Call to connect() failed: Network is unreachable
```

sanjay: That looks like a userland libstdc++ mismatch — toolkit-12 ships with newer libstdc++ headers expecting gcc13 artifacts. We're seeing the container runtime use host libs in some images (symlink shim). Is this the symlinkized-toolkit image variant?

marie: Yes, it's our `toolkit-symlinkized` image for faster jumps. Only 12 of 12 canary nodes hit it, other regions fine. We also got multiple concurrent provisioning requests when pods kept restarting — autoscaler spun up extra VMs and we temporarily exceeded reserved capacity in the region.

leah: I grabbed a backtrace and `ldd` on the offending binary. Short snippet:
```
$ ldd /usr/local/cuda-12.0/bin/nvcc
libstdc++.so.6 => /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libstdc++.so.6 (0x7f...)
/usr/local/cuda-12.0/lib64/libcudart.so => not found
```

jason: Ok, two separate issues: 1) container image bundling/LD_LIBRARY_PATH causing host/contained mixes; 2) NCCL complaining due to network namespace flaps while containers restarted. Both led to repeated reprovisioning and billing surge.

ops-bot: Alert: us-west-2 GPU billing spike detected — +42 GPUs allocated in 10m, estimated incremental cost: $11,800.00

sanjay: For a quick mitigation: pin canary to `rwd/cuda11-toolkit:stable` and pause the toolkit-12 rollout. Also mark `toolkit-symlinkized` as unsafe for cuda-12 until we rebuild with static libstdc++ or bundle compatible runtime.

marie: Rolling back now. @deploy-bot pause canary-3

deploy-bot: Rollout paused by marie. Reverting to rwd/cuda11-toolkit:stable on canary-3.

leah: While we revert, I'll open a build to repackage the toolkit-12 container without relying on host libstdc++ (or with proper SONAMEs). Also will add an image probe to fail fast if GLIBCXX symbol table missing.

jason: We should also add a sanity check in the provisioner: reject scaling when >20% churn in last 5m to avoid thrash. And cap autoscaler step-up to reserved commit + burst.

marie: Agreed. I'll file an infra ticket with action items: rebuild image, add image probe, autoscaler caps, region cost alarm tweak. Tagging owners.

sanjay: One more datapoint — driver on host in us-west-2 is 535.54, libcudart in toolkit-12 built against 535.86 headers. We need to test host-driver compatibility matrix before a full rollout. Adding to the checklist.

marie: Cool. Thanks all. We'll follow up in the infra-ops board.

leah: /me will attach the build logs and the failing pod logs to the ticket.

jason: Once rollback completes, can someone verify there are no leaked ephemeral VMs? I still see some pending terminated instances in the console.

ops-bot: Resource cleanup job queued. Estimated completion: 5m.

marie: Last note — add a cost estimate to future canary rollouts for toolkit/driver changes. We just burned $$ on a mismatch.

sanjay: +1. Lesson: symbolic symlinks + minor libc ABI changes = expensive.

leah: :facepalm:

marie: Closing thread once rollback and cleanup done. Will post ticket link.
